This is why we had the constant problem of water supply.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Unless there are any questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have a question. This is at the very heart of the matter. This topic has already been addressed on several occasions, notably by the Defence of General Praljak. Let me sum up what you just said. Mostar is supplied by two sources, but in the summer there is a problem with one of them because the river is dry. The second source is then used to supply Mostar -- supply water to Mostar, but the supply has to go through pipes, and these pipes absolutely must be controlled by valves. As you said, if there is also air in the pipes, the water pressure can rupture the pipe in the end, and you also said that these pipes go through Rastani. So everything is crystal clear for me. If the BiH Army controls the source from which the pipelines start to supply water to Mostar, then they're probably able to cut the water supply whenever they want to. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The BH Army held Rastani under its control for only a brief period of time. What I wanted to say was that a large stretch of the pipeline was under potential fire from the other side. I came across waterworks workers quite often, and I saw them taking the manholes off. This was in the town. They would take these manholes and took them with them to use as shelter from the fire while they were repairing the pipeline, and I'm talking about the period -- this was in the period when this was under the control of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. I understand what you've just said, but as far as you know, did the ABiH use those pipelines by firing on people to prevent repair for strategy purposes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what the reasons were, but I know that they were repairing ruptured pipes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Another aspect of my question is the following: To your knowledge, the HVO, whether its military aspect or its civilian aspect - I don't know, I won't go into detail - do you think that the HVO tried to prevent water from being supplied to the residents of Mostar and in particular to the residents of East Mostar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The HVO was trying to set up the whole water supply system. Since the bridges were knocked down, there were no technical possibilities for the left bank to be supplied with water, even if they wished to do it. There was no way of doing it. How could they do it? In order to get it to the other bank, you would have to do something, either build bridges or some other construction, which would allow us to place the pipes across the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps this would be a proper moment. I didn't want to interrupt. To your previous question, your previous question was [In English]: "As far as you know, did the ABiH use those pipelines by firing on people to prevent repair, for strategy purposes?" And then the witness, as it is recorded, responded: "I don't know what the reasons were, but I know that they were repairing ruptured pipes." On the Croatian language, as I understood, the witness said, "I don't know what the reasons were, but they were shooting on those people." [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Prlic, you wanted to take the floor. THE ACCUSED PRLIC: [Interpretation] Thank you. Other than that, I lost it on the screen. This is page 51, line 12. The witness said that the workers who went to repair carried or wore the -- were taking the protective metal covers at the time when Rastani were not under the B and H Army control, but here it seems as if they were carrying them when Rastani were under the control, but that doesn't make sense. They did it when it was possible for them to do it. So it was mistranslated on line 18 -- on line 12 of that page and on line 18, as noted by Mr. Kovacic just now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, could you please confirm what you said about those metal covers being taken away by the employees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can confirm that. I can even give you the names of people from the water utility because I saw them in the evening as they were going, once it got dark, so that they wouldn't be seen, and how they are taking the covers from manholes in town in order to protect themselves from shooting by the other side. I remember Mr. Kresic, who was the foreman of that team, and he was also foreman in the water utility in Mostar called Vodovod.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which means that the ABiH was firing at them in order to prevent them from repairing the water pipes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. I was planning on covering those errors, so there was no need for anyone to stand up and get excited. All right. We can now move on to another segment. The next document is 1D 00572, and this is June 26th, 1992. This is a decision to establish a municipal commission for the assessment of war damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My question is: Were you involved in any way with this commission?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first assessment of the war damage was carried out from the Office for Communal and Housing Affairs and Reconstruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to slow down, and I'm going to ask you to listen to my question and try to answer it as briefly and concisely as possible, but please slow down. Otherwise, we make errors, and then people get excited, they jump up, and then, you know, we lose more time. So please. So --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Were you involved in any way with the commission that was making the assessments on the war damage?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next document, 1D 00891.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Could you perhaps, Witness, be a bit more precise in what way you were involved --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah, we will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: -- unless it's on the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We will develop --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- this whole --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me. I withdraw. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The next document is 1D 00891. This is a decision on 30th of June to establish a public enterprise for reconstruction and building of the municipality of Mostar. And are you familiar with this decision?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And how are you familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I participated in its drafting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we go on to the next document, 1D 00437. This is a decision of 16 September 1992 to appoint members to the Municipal Commission for War Damage Assessment, and of course, if you could look at the names. We do see your name on number 14, but very briefly, are there any Muslims appointed to this particular commission? And I might draw your attention to number 5, number 9, and number 13. That may help speed up the process.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of them are Muslims, and they are people that I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. The ones that I -- the numbers that I read out?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Go on to the next document, 1D 02644. This is a decision. We see your name at the bottom of it. It's dated 24 September 1992, and of course, you're asking: "The following shall be appointed to this member of committee for temporary protection of cultural heritage buildings." And by looking at it, it would appear that at least number 1 and number 2, they're Muslims, a construction supervisor and a contractor super -- supervision -- construction supervision and contractor supervision, those two engineers?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1, that's a Muslim; under number 2 is a Muslim; and number 3 is a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And of course under Article number 3, Roman number III, you say that "The commission may hire external consultants, professionals in specific fields, and they shall have the freedom of authority to hire contractors for specific work." What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the engineers who can provide consultations or advisory services and who were supposed to assist the group for the restoration of monuments, which was part of the office that I worked in, in making the assessment about the damage of the old bridge. But also, they were able to perhaps use some funds to do something to protect the old bridge or some other institutions that were also trying to protect the old bridge. They could have assisted them by providing advise and expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Before we move on -- before we move on to the next document, can you tell us whether the old bridge -- whether attempts had been made to protect it during the events with the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You couldn't approach the old bridge at that time because it was under fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about afterwards?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Afterwards, the bridge was shelled. Shells were hitting the bridge, and in order to be able to still use the bridge as a pedestrian bridge, I think the engineers or somebody else perhaps could have assisted there, but I think it was the HVO engineers protected it by placing tyres and planks on it. As far as I can recall, these people from -- who are mentioned here as engineers provided advice to the engineers, the military engineers, on the best way to protect the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you know who the engineers were, the military -- the HVO engineers, and who was under -- who were they subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were not engineers by profession. They were people in the engineering section of the military. I think one of them was called Bozo Pehar, but they were part of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right, thank you. If we look at the next document, 1D 00116, and this is dated December 1992. If we see at the bottom of -- or at the end of this document, this is generated by Dr. Jadranko Prlic. It's a decision on identifying spacial planning, environmental protection, and protection of buildings and their cultural and historical heritage as projects of special importance in the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Are you familiar with this decision, and if so, how?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a decision that was adopted in reference to the company where I was the director.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. What was the purpose of the decision? If you could give us a couple of words.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two main reasons. The first and more important reason was to begin to restore the area in an organised manner, in a planned manner, and cover the other areas of Herzegovina, as well, not just Mostar. Other towns were damaged, as well, and the other settlements, these other municipalities didn't have a company that would be dealing with these issues in order to begin their rebuilding, and Mr. Prlic wanted us to begin reconstruction in other municipalities. The other reason was that I expected that we could make some money in this way outside of Mostar and pay our workers some salary because we didn't receive any salaries from the municipality of Mostar but only some sort of assistance so that we could continue to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we look at the next document, which is 3D 00784, if you could just look at that briefly, and then I'm going to refer you to 1D 02951.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As I understand it, Your Honours, you have it in a separate binder. It is a rather lengthy document. It's approximately 250 pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, first of all, would you confirm -- do you recognise 3D 00784? Do you recognise these pages?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, the document 3D 784, which one is it? Is it the big one, this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes -- no, it's the smaller one. This was introduced a while back, and I will try to -- while the gentleman is looking for it, which should be right -- it's identified as 3D 00798. This is an excerpt, Your Honour, from 1D 02951.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you have 1D 02951, sir? If I could get the usher's assistance --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, it's good if you would tell us so I know. First of all, if you look at -- let's just deal with 1D 02951. What is this? Mostar '92, Urbicide. What is it?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a book called "Urbicide," "Urbici," "Mostar, 1992."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And were you involved in the creation of this book?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wrote a part of the book, and I organised and oversaw the whole project.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What was the purpose of the book?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The purpose of the book was to assess the situation in town and also to show it to the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And where was this exhibited?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an exhibition along with the book as well as a film, "Urbicide 1992." We made a project, Urbicide 1992, consisting of the book, an exhibition, posters, and a film. The entire project toured [Realtime transcript read in error, "toward"] Split, Zagreb, Ljubljana, and the -- was exhibited at the UNESCO Centre in Paris.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And -- I don't have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Karnavas. If I look at the record, the sentence doesn't make sense: "The whole project toward Split, Zagreb, Ljubljana, was exhibited at UNESCO Centre in Paris." After the other towns or --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. The problem is, Your Honour, is the gentleman is speaking rather quickly, and the translators are doing their level best to keep up with the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I don't blame anybody. I'd just like to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, sir, Mr. Puljic, if I could -- we could take it step by step. After this book was created, along with -- this was exhibited along with other material, as I understand it, in various cities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would like to note, instead of "toward," actually I had said "toured," T-O-U-R-E-D.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, the -- where was this exhibit shown? Where was this book exhibited?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Split, in Zagreb, Ljubljana, and in Paris at UNESCO's centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I understand that you were involved in the creation of this book, but who else was involved, and if you could tell us how it was compiled, because we see various photographs of different buildings, monuments, mosques, bridges.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, many engineers from the town of Mostar divided themselves in groups according to topics. They were given the assignment of going around the town, inspecting, and writing something about their particular subject. At the same time, we also employed a number of photographers to take pictures. After that, we made a group that put the whole work together. And as I said, the different parts of the project were put together. Posters were made that were supposed to be put up all over town. A book was made. An exhibition of photographs was created, as well as a film.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And just for technical purposes, Your Honour, a segment of this book was introduced as 3D 00784. We, the Prlic Defence, were under the impression that the entire book at the time had already been introduced. It had not, and we did not put this 1D 02951 on our 65 ter list. So at this point in time or after the witness finishes, we would be tendering this to be added to our list of exhibits, and I understand that the Praljak Defence team may also be doing the same in the eventuality that the Trial Chamber denies our request. All right. If we can move on to just one last document in this segment, 1D 02237.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, we don't have a date on this particular document. It talks about -- we see a headline: "Love is a reflection of the world." It's from a newspaper clipping, and it's an exhibition of paintings by Mostar artists. Do you know what this is being referenced to, and about what time are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can you help us out?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the Urbicide exhibition in Split, a concert was organised at the same time at the Stadium Lud [phoen] and also an exhibition of Mostar painters. This whole event was used to collect funds for the rebuilding of Mostar bridges, and it included the exhibition Urbicide, the exhibition of Mostar painters, and the concert at the stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And these artists that are noted in the article, from what particular nationality are they?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of all nationalities, but for the most part, Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we go on to the next topic and last topic, and it's just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before we move to the last topic, Witness, I'd like to go back to the old bridge. We've seen documents establishing that the HVO had taken the necessary measures to protect the old bridge, and you also provided a detail that I didn't know; that it was your employees under the supervision of your engineers who protected the old bridge with tyres, planks, and so on. We know, in document 1D 2951 -- we learn in that document that you've shown the world, at least to the UNESCO organisation in Paris, the damage caused in Mostar during the conflict with the Serbs. This leads me to the following question: In 1993, there was a conflict in Mostar between the HVO and the ABiH, and at one stage we heard evidence according to which, via a video excerpt, a tank apparently under HVO control fired in the direction of the old bridge. The old bridge collapsed. We're trying to determine why the bridge collapsed. But at any rate, at one particular stage we see a tank belonging apparently to the HVO shooting at the bridge. How can you explain this particular event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also saw the tank on television. Perhaps I saw it on television. I don't know. In what sense are you seeking my explanation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just like everyone else, you saw this tank shooting at the bridge. You saw this on television. According to you -- I mean, you were living in Mostar at the time. Are there any reasons to fire at that bridge? Was there a reason behind this, or was it just madness? Was it totally illogical?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was sorry that they fired at the old bridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you have no comments to make. Okay, fine. Let's move on to this last topic, Mr. Karnavas. Let me tell you that you've used four hours and thirteen minutes so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just one -- I need to go back and make one correction. Apparently on page 53, line 18, Mr. President, you had asked a question, and the question was -- says: "Which means that the HVO --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: "Which means that the HVO was firing at them in order to stop them from repairing the water pipes." And I want to make sure that we hear it from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was it the HVO that was firing at the repairmen, or was it the ABiH that was firing at the repairmen who were trying to fix the water pipes?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay, now if we turn --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In my question, it was ABiH. It wasn't the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But it's in the record, and, you know, we do panic about things like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The last topic deals with a seminar that was held in Neum. If we could look at 1D 02703. If you could -- 1D 02703, and there are a series of documents that actually relate to this seminar. Do you have it, sir?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We see that it was held on 22nd and 23rd April, 1993, and from the top -- at the top of the page, we see "University of Mostar." At the time, sir, was that the name of the university in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it was called, university in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, okay. University of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, prior to that, did it have a name, a different name?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was called Dzemal Bijedic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, we see that there was this seminar, and if we look at number -- page 2, we don't see your name on this list, but do you know the individuals that are listed as the board of organisers and the editorial board?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know most of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And are there any Muslims on either the board of organisers or the editorial board?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among the organisers, under number 3, Professor/Dr. Faruk Pavlovic. Under number 7, Professor Mehmed Behmen. I think he was the dean of the Mechanical Engineering Faculty. Under number 8, Professor Nerkez Mackic, who was, I believe, the dean of the Construction Engineering College. And then under number 10, Nijaz Bajgoric. On the editorial board, there was Professor Himzo Djukic and Professor Elvedin Hanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, in this particular seminar, did you participate?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And just briefly, and if you could confirm whether you were familiar with the documents that were presented at this seminar. Let's look at 1D 02704. This is by Jadranko Prlic, "Fundamental Guidelines for the Global Economic Developments in Herceg-Bosna." Next, 1D 02705. This is by a Mr. Dziho and Miscevic [phoen], "Wartime Damage and Instructions for the Reconstruction of the Architectural Heritage of Mostar." These two individuals, are they Croat, Muslim, Serb, or what are they?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to document number -- Dziho is a Muslim, and Tanja, I don't know how she declared herself, but her father is a Serb and her mother a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then we see 1D 02706, "Overview of the Problems of Destruction, Reconstruction, and Development of Towns in Herceg-Bosna," and we see "Urbicide," and then we see at the top your name. Is this your -- the paper that you prepared?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we just look at page 2 in the English version, under table 1, we do see -- you have some figures there. For instance, if we were to go to "Bridges," and it says that before the war, there are 13; damaged, 1; destroyed, 11; intact, 1. And then you give a percentage of 92. Were those figures correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And would you stand by the other figures related to the hotels, municipal buildings? For instance, municipal buildings, we see none are intact. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I stand by all the figures listed here. And, second of all, let me correct you. Municipal buildings, before the war, there were five of them. One of them was damaged, and four of them were absolutely destroyed, and none of them were intact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Apparently I was mistranslated, so sorry, but I'm glad to see that you're paying attention. All right. Would you confirm to us whether these documents, these presentations were made in Neum on the 22nd and 23rd of April, 1993, having participated at this seminar?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The documents were all compiled in a book, which we received at the seminar as part of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know what the purpose of the seminar was?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The country was destroyed, and the purpose of the seminar was to gather all the individuals who had expertise in certain areas, primarily members of universities but also outside of universities, in order to think about the direction the future development of the country should take, or the directions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I just want to go through one last document. It's not related to the seminar, but its 1D 02065, because we see the seminar was held on the 22nd and 23rd of April, 1993. This document relates to 6 May 1993 or shortly thereafter, and this is a statement from a Mr. Lasic. Do you know Mr. Lasic?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know Mr. Lasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And perhaps you can provide us with a comment or two. It says here at the very top: "Despite all agreements at the highest level between General Petkovic and Halilovic and at the level of the Southeastern Herzegovina Operational Zone and the BH Army 4th Corps, some representatives of the BH Army want at all costs to cause a conflict between HVO and the BH Army, i.e., between the Croatian and Muslim people, which is evident from the following examples:" And they give one example on 5 May 1993. Now -- related to two individuals. Are you familiar with the events that are being described here that had occurred on 5 May 1993?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, TV broadcasts reported on certain negotiations or agreements, and this is what the situation was like on the ground. I do recall this particular event when the two young men were arrested. That's what the situation was like throughout the period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, in paragraph number 2, there is a mentioning of a Zuka. Do you know that person? Who was he?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met him once.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And -- okay, do you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the commanders of the BH Army, which was, in effect, a Muslim army. When I got to know him, he wore very expensive clothes, he had expensive glasses, and an expensive Jeep. He had a large flag that was flaunting from his Jeep. This took place in Konjic 'round about this time, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What did the flag look like?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a green flag with some Arabic writing I couldn't decipher.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were those the coat of arms of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Negotiations were taking place at the time. I was part of a delegation going for negotiations to Jablanica and Konjic. A member of the delegation was Mr. Pusic. With us, there were also representatives of the BH Army from Mostar. The purpose of our trip was to try and conduct negotiations in order to reintroduce peace, to introduce a ceasefire.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When was that, about what month and year?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the date. It was, let's say, in May 1993, precisely at the time this document was drafted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, just as a vignette, because I think the story is rather interesting, could you please describe exactly what happened at that meeting? And I mean, go into the details, before Mr. Zuka arrives and what happens when he arrives.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Petar Zelenika tasked me with being a member of a delegation, the purpose of which was to conduct negotiations in Jablanica and Konjic. The delegation included Mr. Pusic, Mr. Raguz, and me on the Croat side. On the Muslim side, there were two officers of their army. Those of us from Mostar were supposed to go to Jablanica and Konjic to try as a mixed delegation to bring about the calming down of the situation. As we reached Jablanica under the escort of the Spanish members of UNPROFOR, we stayed there for a while, negotiating. Mr. Blago Pusic joined a member of the BH Army and went to Doljani to try and calm the situation down through negotiations, and we carried on in the direction of Konjic. Having got there, we got out of the APC and were immediately surrounded by throngs of people. It was an unruly crowd led by a soldier, Zuka. I recall him very well because he spoke the Ekavian version, E-K. And they were shouting at us, jeering at us, throwing stones at us, and this soldier took out a knife and threatened to cut our throats. There were only two members of the Spanish unit of UNPROFOR standing between us and the crowd. One of the two officers went to the APC in order to radio for reinforcements. At the point this man was approaching me - when I say "me," I mean me and Mr. Raguz and other members of the BH Army and this officer with his knife - the car I've just described to you arrived. There was this large green flag with Arabic writing attached to the car, and it was so big that it was dragging along the road. The person who subsequently introduced himself as Zuka got out of the car. As his car showed up, everybody stood in their tracks. We were backing up a wall, and then there was this Spanish soldier in front of us, and as Zuka arrived he cast a glance at the crowd, which suddenly fell completely silent. Not a word was uttered. The crowd dispersed, and the soldier returned his knife to the sheath. At that point, Spanish UNPROFOR troops appeared, and then Mr. Zuka asked us and the Spaniards to join him in his headquarters in Konjic. We then -- they then started to talk. The conversation was conducted in Spanish. Let me point out this as an interesting thing. The BH Army officer at that point took out a piece of paper from his pocket, which read, and this is something that he read aloud: "Mr. Zuka, I am here according to the command of Mr. Arif Pasalic, commander of the 4th Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina." Zuka took the note and theatrically ripped it into small pieces. He then said, "By the order of the commander-in-chief, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, I hereby command all of the army from" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] ... "all the way to Neum."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From where to where?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Igman, meaning from Sarajevo, to Neum.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Puljic. With that, I have no further questions. I want to thank you very, very much, and I take it you will be equally as forthcoming in your answers to all questions coming from whichever direction. Thank you again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Before moving forward, I think we should have a second break, so we will break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Court is back in session, and I will ask the other Defence teams whether they have any questions to ask during cross-examination. Did you, Ms. Nozica, any questions? No questions?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. The Defence for Mr. Stojic will have questions for this witness, but the Defence -- or, rather, my learned friend Madam Alaburic will start first. But before that, Your Honours, since the direct examination by my learned friend Mr. Karnavas has been prolonged, can you tell the total time the Defence might have in excess to what they have been allowed so far? I know that three Defence teams are interested in examining -- cross-examining the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. As we said in the guidelines, Defence will have 50 per cent of the time, so you have two hours altogether. Since there are three of you, you have two hours for the three of you. The Prosecution will be granted four hours for its cross-examination, and it's going to be a very tight schedule given the time left if we want to make sure our witness doesn't stay over the weekend. So it's Ms. Alaburic, Ms. Nozica. Who is the third that wanted to take the floor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the third Defence is the Defence for Mr. Praljak. My colleague, Madam Nika Pinter, will have some questions to ask, and then my client, Mr. Praljak, will have a few questions as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you distribute the time among yourselves; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, by your leave, I should first like to greet you, Mr. Puljic, and all the colleagues in the courtroom. We have agreed in principle about the distribution of time, and I believe that the two hours will suffice for the three Defence teams. We decided to divide the time in equal shares, and should the situation change, we will consult in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You have one hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Puljic, hello to you once more. Let me ask you at the outset -- I would kindly ask the interpreter that we are starting with the cross-examination of Vesna Alaburic. Mr. Puljic, let us first acquaint Their Honours with our personal relationship. Have you ever met me? Have we ever talked to each other? Have I taken a part in the preparations for your testimony here?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I see you, and I've never spoken to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me first inform you of the topics I should like to discuss with you. All these topics were the subject of the direct examination conducted by the Prlic Defence. If need be, I will present you with certain documents. All these documents were either used by the Defence team for Mr. Prlic or were prepared by that same Defence team for your testimony. In this way, you will not be surprised by any of these documents. The topics will be as follows: Your explanation about the civilian and military authorities in Mostar between March and June 1992; next, I should like the two of us to analyse a decision of the Crisis Staff taken on the 29th of April, 1992, whereby the Defence tasks are entrusted with the HVO. Then I will have a question about your statement concerning mobilisation and war hospital. Let us start with the topic of the civilian and military authorities. Yesterday, you told us that the civilian authorities in Mostar did not function, this is at page 65 of the transcript; that the Crisis Staff de facto was unable to do anything, pages 18 and 69 of the transcript; that neither -- that -- or, rather, that the special-purpose council was not able to do anything, either, that's at page 69; and that in the prevailing situation of chaos, the only functioning body was the HVO, that's page 78 of yesterday's transcript. Tell me, Mr. Puljic, did I -- is this a fair understanding -- a correct understanding of what you'd been saying yesterday?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us closely define the terms "civilian" and "military authorities," and let us define what the situation was like in the individual months of the period we're interested in. I don't think it's contested that as of March 1992 -- as at March 1992, Bosnia-Herzegovina was one of the states forming part of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you explain which were the civilian authorities that existed in Bosnia-Herzegovina, including those, of course, in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just as in any other state, there existed three levels of authority; legislative, executive and judicial.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: These are not levels of authority. These are types of authority. Would you agree with me that there existed three levels, the federative, republican and municipal?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, at the municipal level, who was vested with the role of the legislative body?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Assembly was the legislative body.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Who had the role of the government at municipal level?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Executive Committee or Board of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What was the colloquial term used for the president of the Executive Board of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: President of the Municipal Board.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Was that person sometimes referred to as mayor, regardless of the fact that officially such a title or such a role did not exist?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. That was the case, for instance, in Croatia. That's why I asked. When we're talking about the military authorities of the time, can you tell me, what is your understanding of the term "military authority"?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say "authority," you think of someone who has clout, power. Let me give you a small detail that might illustrate --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: No, no, please. We won't have time for that. When you say that in your understanding "military authority" implies someone who has power, power to do what?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To do any sort of activity. In order to do something, you not only have to wish to do that, but you also have to have the power to do it. For instance, the JNA was able to do things because it had power.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could we then say that in some way, when it comes to the military aspect, the Yugoslav People's Army had a certain power and certain functions?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, the JNA was under the control of the Federation, of the federal state of Yugoslavia, was it not?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Likewise, did the Territorial Defence have a certain power to wield?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In peacetime, it didn't have any power. It had potential power, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, was the Territorial Defence under the control of the republics or some other sociopolitical organisation?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything you've been asking me about so far is beyond the field of my expertise and falls under the headline of, let's say, general knowledge. And from what I know about it, as general knowledge, the Territorial Defence was within the framework of republics.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, did republican secretariats for national defence exist within individual republics?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did there exist municipal secretariats for national defence in municipalities?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Were they civilian bodies dealing with certain affairs from the field of national defence?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were civilian bodies concerned with certain matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did these civilian bodies have certain powers in relation to the issue of defence?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't have power or authority. They executed the tasks that they received from the JNA. This is an assumption on my part. I cannot give you a full answer to the question as I understand it. I think that they were there to execute certain tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, who could order them to carry out certain tasks? The republican -- when we're talking about the republican and municipal secretariats for national defence, are you sure that the JNA had the power to order them to carry out any sort of task?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is outside my knowledge. However, as the people viewed it, the JNA was omnipotent.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you recall whether on the 3rd of March, 1992, Bosnia-Herzegovina declared its independence?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can we take that day to be the start of an open war against the JNA, or rather, between the JNA and the Army of the -- rather, yes, against the JNA and against the army of Bosnian-Herzegovinian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that we can.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Is that the time when complete chaos started to reign across the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was chaos before that, as well, but it intensified at the time, which is quite clear and obvious.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In the month of March 1992, there yet did not exist a body that would be called the Croatian Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In March 1992 --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you that. I would have to see the document stating when the Croatian Defence Council was set up.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I've prepared these documents for you. There's no need to look at that. I can only refer Their Honours to P151, a document dated the 8th of April, 1992, and document P155, dated the 10th of April, 1992, a decision taken by Mate Boban about the HVO becoming the supreme body of defence. We will not be going into that now, but in April 1992, the first bodies bearing the name of the Croatian Defence Council were set up. Mr. Puljic, you were discussing P135, dated the 12th of March, 1992. This is an invitation of the president -- or this is an invitation to the president of the Presidency -- rather, the president of the Assembly of Mostar, which was scheduled for the 3rd of March, this session. You said that it was decided at the time, due to chaos and the impossibility of work, the Assembly should be dissolved and the Crisis Staff of Mostar set up instead; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, the Crisis Staff in Mostar, was it civilian or military authority?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilian.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, at that time in mid-March 1992, constituted the military authority in Mostar [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a time of chaos. Anyone who held a certain territory constituted a military authority.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Puljic, when you say "military authority," that has to be a body or a person or a group of people who have the power to do something. And as you spoke about the military power in Mostar at that period, I'm asking you: Who did you mean? Which body is this? Who are these people who had the military power?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The JNA had the military power on the left bank, and to the north in the barracks of the JNA the army had the military power. And in the other areas, you had local units of the HVO, which at that time, in the military sense, controlled the territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Are you sure that all of these units were called "HVO"? I'm talking about March 1992.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that they did, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, did the Independent Battalion exist at that time, the one that we talked about?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, I would just like to remind you of documents shown to you by the Prlic Defence. This is document 1D -- no need to look. You will remember. 1D 1572. That is that report by Arif Pasalic, "100 Days of War," which states that the Independent Battalion was founded on the 12th of April. You, as far as I can recall, confirmed the accuracy of the information in that report, and it turns out on the basis of what is said in that battalion -- that report that the battalion did not exist in March. So in your opinion and in view of the circumstances, what do you think? Did the battalion, the Independent Battalion, exist or not in March 1992?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me about details that I cannot know anything about. What I do know is that the SDA also was arming a part of its people, that there were organised small groups, and all of these units were organised locally in neighbourhoods, in villages. So you can say that the Independent Battalion was organised somewhere in the area of the old city.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you name anyone who would be representing this military authority, a person that would have that kind of military power? Can you think of anyone at that time? I'm talking about March 1992. If you don't remember, we can just move on. It was a long time ago. Can I conclude that you don't remember, that you don't know?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know a lot of people. I know a lot of people in town, and I know that a lot of them were in the HVO. I mean, I cannot really mention all of their names, who at that time had joined the defence of the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Well, that is not controversial. I'm talking about military authority, people who had military authority. You mentioned that term, that concept, and I wanted to describe that or go into it in more detail. So can we now conclude that you are not aware of any people who had that sort of military authority in Mostar at that time?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commanders of the HVO at the time had military authority.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us who the HVO commanders were, some names?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jadran Topic, Petar Zelenika, Rade Bosnjak, Slavko Puljic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Tell us, Jadran Topic, which military unit was he in command of?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, if you know, whether he was in command of any military unit?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think he was one of the main people in the staff, and he simply was not in a position to control a -- to command a specific military formation or unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at document 1D 2389. You also have it in my set of documents. This is a document appointing the council for the special purposes of the Mostar Municipal Staff. Can we look at the person who signed the document? That is Jadran Topic. He signed the document, and his post or function is named "President." Do you see that, Mr. Puljic? It's the last document in my set of documents, and they have been arranged, and you can also see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So his post is named "President." And now, Mr. Puljic, can you please explain to us, the functions entitled "President," were they functions of the civilian authority or of the military authority?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Functions called -- with the title "President" are functions of the civilian authority.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So based on the signature and the name of the post, can we conclude that Jadranko Topic as president of the Municipal Staff of Mostar was a representative of the civilian authority?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's hard to conclude that. In order to conclude that, I would need to know how literate were the people who were drafting all these things.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. We will look at some of the documents, and then we will see.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who were preparing these documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The documents where somebody signs themselves with the title "Commander," "zapovjednik," or, for example, "Chief of the Main Staff," according to what you know, are these signatures of persons carrying out some sort of military function?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question in view of the fact that all the questions are at a theoretical level where one would need to be precise. And we're speaking about a specific situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm also referring to a very specific situation. I'm asking you about documents that somebody would sign as a commander of the 1st Brigade, for example. Is that a concept or a term of a commander, and is that related to some sort of military function?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Well, let us now look at the next document, document P209. That is also a document that you have already seen, the document brought by Jadranko Topic as the president of the Crisis Staff. The document says that the Crisis Staff is being disbanded, thereby ending all of its functions as a representative of the civilian power. Can you please tell us, well, does this document confirm your thesis that the Crisis Staff was a civilian authority; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff was a civilian authority.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Under item 2, the formation of a civilian wartime government is being announced; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: From the time of the disbanding of the Crisis Staff until the formation of the civilian war government, the functions of the civilian authority were supposed to be carried out by the special-purposes council of the HVO of the Municipal Staff of Mostar as stated in Article -- or paragraph 3; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it states.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And then we have a decision of the 21st of May, 1992, and that is a document P221, which appoints members of the Croatian Defence Council of the municipality of Mostar. Can you please tell us, here we're talking about the Croatian Defence Council of the municipality of Mostar, and they are civilian authorities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, just let me find this decision. Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You can see it on the screen. You can recognise that document. You talked about them, so there is no need to lose time in looking for the document.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the decision on the formation of the civilian authority.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can we look at item 12, Jasmin Jaganjac, who is the head of the defence department; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So from this decision, it follows that Jasmin Jaganjac is a member of the civilian authority?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I would now, Mr. Puljic, like us to correct the erroneous translation of a document which you discussed with the Defence of Mr. Prlic today, so I would like to ask you in their segment of documents to find document 1D 1217. It's a report of the Municipal Staff for Civilian Protection about the implementation of tasks in the sphere of civilian protection in the region of the town of Mostar for the 60 days of the war. On page 3, lines 9 to 15 of today's [as interpreted] report, the question of Mr. Karnavas was noted down which was quite correctly based on the translation, but the translation is incorrect. So in the English text, and that is what the question states, it is said -- I'm going to read it in English: [In English] "Since the work of the civilian authorities was not organised at the beginning of the war... " [Interpretation] And so on and so forth, end of quotation. Mr. Puljic, I would now like you to look at this text in the Croatian language. This is on page 2, beginning of the second whole paragraph. I would like you to read that, to read the beginning of that sentence.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In view of the fact that the civilian authority in the early period of the war functioned in an unorganised manner ... "

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can we agree, then, that the civilian authority did exist at the beginning of the war, but it functioned in a disorganized way? That is what it says in this report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So we cannot say that in June 1992, there was no civilian authority in Mostar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We cannot say that for June.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Yes. This report is from June, and we see that the civilian authority was organised on the 21st of May. It adopted a series of decisions, and then we could see that it would be wrong to conclude, and we can see that on the basis of this report, to say that there was no civilian authority in Mostar in June 1992?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The civilian authority did exist in the month of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. I would now like you to explain this. Jadran Topic was the first-ranking person of the civilian authority in Mostar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at document P485. It's a document signed by Jadran Topic dated the 16th of September, 1992. In the document, there is a decision that all documents that refer to the words "Territorial Defence," these words should be substituted for the term "Croatian Defence Council," and then it is established that the Independent Battalion, which is active in the Mostar municipality area, is part, by establishment, of the formations of the Croatian Defence Council. Did you find that document?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us whether -- we apologise to the interpreters. Mr. Puljic, can you please tell us based on the first paragraph of this decision it follows that the municipal civilian authority made some decisions that had to do with territorial defence, or rather, the Croatian Defence Council; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. And then the second segment indicates that the civilian authority in Mostar makes decisions on which battalion will be in the establishment formation of the HVO of the municipality of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it states here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. I'm now going to remind you of three documents which were shown to you yesterday by Mr. Prlic's Defence. There is no need for you to look because I'm going to just tell you about it. I'm only interested in one thing. These are documents 1D 583, a decision of the 30th of June, 1992, signed by Jadran Topic on the temporary suspension of work of catering establishment; the second document is 1D 584, same person issued it on the same date, on the work hours of companies and retail establishments, the same person, on the same day. And then we have the third document, 1D 586, decision issued by the same person on the same date about a curfew. In each of these decisions, it is said that the military police, among other bodies, will be responsible for the implementation of this decision. What I would like you to do for us, Mr. Puljic, is to explain to us if Mr. Jadran Topic was authorised to issue tasks to the military police in terms of implementing certain aspects of municipal decisions or whether he was able to give assignments to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you're asking me here is something that you would need to call in experts in this field who will give you an opinion. I see my role as a witness who will testify about facts, so I would kindly like to ask the Court not to be asked to provide my opinions or to think about anything that has to do with Mr. Topic. Please ask me about facts.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the question by the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I have to repeat what my learned friend promptly and normally says. As you both speak the same language, you have a tendency to overlap; that is to say, when one has heard the answer, she or he goes on speaking. And now, for instance, your question has gotten lost to the interpreters, and we lose time because they have to -- you have to repeat it. It's an old story. Temperament carries one away. Please, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for your caution. I think that Mr. Puljic and I are both trying to pause and to slow down, but I hope this will not happen again.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Puljic, as an individual who drafted the decision of the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Mostar dated the 29th of April, 1992, which is P180, please provide us a couple of explanations in relation to the decision, which you do recall, don't you?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You told us that you drafted the decision, that you saw the HVO's attempts to protect and defend the town, which was the reason why you wanted to make an assessment of the current situation, put it on paper, and ask the HVO to defend your town; is this a fair interpretation of your words?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us try to analyse the decision together, if we can. I suppose we shall agree that in item 1, you wanted to define the enemy.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In item 2, you decide that for the affairs of -- that, rather, the tasks of protection and defence of the city will be entrusted to the Croatian Defence Council, municipal headquarters Mostar, and members of the Ministry of the Interior; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In other words, the defence was not only entrusted to the HVO but also to the MUP?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In item 3, you indicate that the Croatian Defence Council shall consist of the members of Muslim and Croat peoples and members of other peoples and minorities. Is this your stipulation of who can become a member of the HVO? Is this where you say that members of the HVO can become -- or rather, that Croats, Muslims, and everybody else that wishes to can become a member of the HVO; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we were doing here was to make an assessment of the current situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, did the HVO, in other -- was the HVO in other parts of Herceg-Bosna, as well, being created at the time as a joint army of Bosnian -- of Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't be able to give you an answer to that question because at that time Mostar to me was the entire world.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: At the time you drafted this decision and earlier on, did it ever occur to you that there might break out a conflict between Muslims and Croats which, in fact, did break out a year later?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When one drafts a decision, one drafts it on the principles of one's own honesty, and I believe that it was honestly written.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I don't think that's been called into doubt by anyone, that this was written honestly, but I suppose at the time you were drafting this decision neither you nor the individuals you consulted in drafting this decision could even have a hunch of what might happen between Muslims and Croats a year later; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In item 5, you define the task of the Croatian Defence Council; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You also set forth that the Croatian Defence Council should make sure that its members act in such a way that the Mostar residents are guaranteed their security and safety. So you're talking about a duty on the part of the Croatian Defence Council; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Likewise, you stipulate that this particular role should be played by the military police; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In item 6, you indicate the importance of the running of the judiciary; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The decision indicates what should be done in the future.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In item 7, you speak of the necessity to coordinate the work of individual bodies in Mostar, which should also work jointly; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Is it your view, Mr. Puljic, that by this decision on the HVO in Mostar, you set out clearly and precisely the instructions on how the HVO should do what?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We expressed our wishes as the civilian authority. But on the other side, there should be the HVO to accept that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, Mr. Puljic, you said that you drafted the decision. If you wanted to express your wishes only, how come you used the following formulations: It is the task of the HVO, the HVO is duty-bound to, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were giving ourselves airs a bit and overstating our significance.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Right. That is one of the possible interpretations. Another is that you did have that significance, but we will not go into that. Let me put a question to you concerning your answer on mobilisation. That's at page 18 of yesterday's transcript. You said that municipalities were unable to conduct mobilisation, although there was a defence office in place. You said that the defence office was able to carry out mobilisation only pursuant to an order from the military bodies. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what period this statement of yours refers to?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The prewar period. From the point the war started and chaos ensued, I can't really give you an answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: "The prewar period" would imply sometime until the month of March 1992? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, let's put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, if you know, was this regulated by a federal piece of legislation on defence or by a BH law on defence?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, what is your source of knowledge about the fact that a military body had to issue an order in order for the defence office to carry out mobilisation? Where does this information you have come from?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We couldn't issue any sort of an order for mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We're talking about the prewar period, aren't we, prior to March? Who could have issued an order for mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which state body could have done that, but it must have been a state body or the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have any further questions. Mr. Puljic, I thank you. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We have 15 minutes left, and I will now give the floor to the second counsel. Ms. Nozica, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon once more. Can I have the usher's assistance in taking these documents to Their Honours, the Prosecutor and the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I should also like to start my examination by greeting you first, Mr. Puljic. Let me also ask you if in the course of your preparation for the current testimony you met anyone from the Defence team of Mr. Stojic, whether you were in touch in any way with me, and whether you are familiar with the documents I'd like to examine you on.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never met you, and this is the first time I see the documents. I know Mr. Stojic because he was the manager of the public utility company in Neum at the time I worked there, and we worked in the same building.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Mr. Puljic, I have prepared a binder for you, which I hope will be easy for you to find your way in. Let me inform Their Honours that I will be examining the witness only about the topics that were the subject of direct examination. Mr. Puljic, His Honour Judge Antonetti asked you today during your direct examination - that's at page 31, lines 4 to 17 - he asked you whether the service you were at the head of undertook any sort of activities to repair the buildings which were damaged or destroyed before the start of the conflict between the HVO and the BH Army, that's to say the damage that ensued from Serb activity, and your answer was that you didn't have time to. My question to you is: Did you make sure that you create plans that would cover the entire territory of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were making plans for the reconstruction of many damaged and destroyed buildings, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I am waiting for the interpretation. I might even lose sight of that and start rushing, but I believe we should try and take it slowly. I should like you to look at the first document in the binder. This is part of the indictment. You have to forget about it for the time being. Look at document 2D 1422. 2D 1422. This is the SOS for Mostar document. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Puljic, tell us first if you remember this document at all.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Can we conclude that this is a document of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Croatian Defence Council, Mostar municipality, is that right? And this is an SOS for Mostar addressed to construction companies, manufacturers of construction materials, food production companies, businessmen, Mostar business partners, friends of Mostar and Herzegovina? Paragraph 1 speaks of the liberation of the town of Mostar from the Serbian aggression. Paragraph 2 says that a battle is being fought for the temporary repair or reconstruction and the return of citizens. And now it says: "On Thursday, the 17th of September, 1992, at 1500 hours, at the Brijuni Sports Hall, on the first level next to the main entrance to the Zagreb International Fair, a 15-minute footage will be broadcast for the first time, and we're expecting to be invited to this gathering." Mr. Puljic, would this particular invitation have to do with the activity you referred to, which was part of an effort on your part to try and raise funds to reconstruct what had been destroyed in Mostar during the Serb aggression?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not my activity or the activity on the part of the public enterprise for the reconstruction and construction of Mostar. I do know, however, that at the same time various individuals, various institutions were engaged in this particular activity. Everyone was trying to give a contribution of their own.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You say "to give a contribution of their own," but to complete the sentence, tell us, to give a contribution in what? In the reconstruction of what had been destroyed in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let us look at the second document in my binder, 1D 2367. You probably recognise this document.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Then please tell us what it's all about.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the Zagreb Architectural Faculty, we presented an exhibit -- the exhibition called "The Mostar Urbicide," along with a book that was published on the same topic. To that exhibition, we invited representatives of the BH Embassy in Zagreb, and we invited the prime minister of Bosnia-Herzegovina. They came to the opening of the exhibition, and I thanked them for it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So was there any interest on the part of the community to help reconstruct Mostar?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the purpose was to inform them of the extent of the destruction in Mostar, but also to call on the public to give their contributions.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let us recall everyone that this took place on the 15th of January, 1993. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Your effort to try and bring about the reconstruction of Mostar carried on into 1993; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Puljic, at that point in time when the book entitled "Urbicide" was made, can we conclude that at that point, the Islam or the Muslim heritage that existed in Mostar had largely, by that time, been destroyed? And I mean the buildings that had to do with the Islamic or Muslim heritage. I'm speaking of cultural monuments.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right, but only partly. On the left bank, next to the Islamic Cultural Heritage, most of the buildings were the legacy of the Austro-Hungarian empire, and these buildings were also destroyed. On the left bank, there was the Serb Orthodox --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, I know that. We will get back to that later, to the Serb Orthodox Church. But when you say "on the left bank," let us be more precise, then. On the left bank, a great many facilities were destroyed of great importance to the Islamic region -- religion and culture; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.
