utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you to move to document 2D 1418, and that is the third document in the binder. It's a letter written by Bishop Peric. I assume that you'd never seen this letter before, but I'm also quite sure that you know what it says. I'm sure you are familiar with these particular circumstances. For the transcript, first of all, you tell me, you knew Bishop Peric?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you have contacts with him during the war?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And this letter is written on the 13th of December, 1993, to Mr. Perica Jukic and to Mr. Jozo Maric. Did you know these gentlemen?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We don't have the time, unfortunately, to read the whole letter. You can just glance at it, and I'm going to draw your attention to key sections. This is a letter in which Bishop Peric asks Mr. Jukic and Mr. Maric that the following facilities be protected. They are buildings that are important for those of the Islamic faith and those of the Orthodox faith. And in the beginning, they provide the description of occupied counties, and that is on this page listed under paragraphs 1, 2, 3. I assume you would need to know that. This is the list of occupied parishes, those religious buildings of the Catholic Church that were burned, torn down, or heavily and lightly damaged; then under 2, a list of destroyed buildings that belonged to the Serbian Orthodox Church, and this is of July 1992, and then it says that: "Our response is in the voice of councils"; and then under 3, photocopy of the list of destroyed buildings that belonged to the Islamic religious community, "which I already received in January of 1993." My question in relation to this document, and then we're going to go through each of these three lists so that you can recall what you know about them. So in terms of this document, my question is: Are you aware that during the war, the whole war, because this is the end of 1993, Bishop Peric advocated the protection of all religious buildings and urged that the truth be established about how those religious-purpose buildings were destroyed?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is something that I know about, not only from his public addresses, but also privately he equally advocated the protection of buildings that had a religious use, regardless of who they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we look at this list of counties and parishes where there was discretion, and this is in paragraph 1, and it's document 2D 01419. Can you please just look at that list, and can you please tell us if you think that this corresponds to what you know about the destroyed buildings from the counties and parishes and that were destroyed during the war in the course of 1993?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This does correspond to what I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. The third document is of most interest to me, about the Islamic religious buildings and mosques, and that is why we're going to look at 2D 1417. That is the next document in your binder. This is a letter that you perhaps have seen before. First of all, we have a letter from Patriarch Pavle and the Bishop of Mostar, Zanic [phoen], to Boutros-Ghali, and that is the first paragraph in the Croatian version that you have. We also have the second response by Bishop Peric regarding allegations of destroyed Serbian buildings. Can you please look at this? First of all, the Orthodox cathedral in Mostar is being referred to; the reply by Mr. Peric; then we have the Orthodox churches in Capljina and Metkovic. So did these buildings suffer damage in the war? Do you have any information about this?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these buildings were damaged in the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is one of those letters that Bishop Peric refers to in document 2D 1418. I would now like us all to look at the third list. I probably will not have enough time to go through it in detail. That would be this third list of buildings of the Islamic community that were destroyed during the war. That is document 2D 1421. Have you seen this document?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm looking at it now. I'm seeing it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you just go through the list of ruined or destroyed mosques in Mostar, and there is a description "Major destruction." I am stressing it for the transcript, which you can see on page 2 at the bottom that this is a document from January 1993. Bishop Peric received it in January, which would seem to indicate - and you can confirm if I'm right - that this is destruction that was sustained during the Serb aggression.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the indicated mesjids were destroyed during the Serbian aggression.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I assume that I need to finish now, so I would like to put one more question to the witness as an introduction on our continued work on this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you please explain to the Trial Chamber the difference between a mosque and a mesjid, if you do know the difference, and I assume that you do.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A mosque has a mihrab and a mimber.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I don't think that you said enough.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm going to translate. When you enter a mosque, you have the mihrab. That is the section where the priest performs the prayer, And mimber is the place -- actually, it's a staircase that is above the mihrab where you would give a sermon.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And does a mosque have a minaret?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does, but this is the main difference. A mesjid does not have a mimber. It only has a mihrab where prayers are performed. There are no sermons. That is the main difference. Most frequently, mosques have wells, and very often mesjids do not.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I think that I need to stop here. Thank you very much, sir. We will continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You have used up 16 minutes. 2D has used 16 minutes. It's almost 10 to 2.00. But tomorrow we'll meet at 9.00. Have a nice day. See you tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 17th day of September, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
